Bounds.description:
A justified interval for an estimate.

``lower_w`` and ``upper_w`` are nullable (HB §18).  When both are present
the validator requires ``lower_w <= upper_w``.  A zero-width interval
(a point) is only possible through the private :meth:`_point` constructor,
which represents an IDENTIFIABLE or MEASURED result; the ``allow_point``
flag is *not* a field and never appears in the model or its JSON schema.
Bounds.title: Bounds

EstimateStatus.description: What kind of value an estimate is (HB §8.5).
EstimateStatus.title: EstimateStatus

PowerLevel.description:
Which of a device's four power levels a published value belongs to.

``06-device-and-load-model-spec.md`` §5.1 names four levels -- standby,
idle, active, transient -- and ``ExpectedPower`` carries the envelope
(``standby_w``, ``idle_w``, ``on_w``, ``startup_w`` / ``shutdown_w``).
This enum is the label a *published* value carries.

It is a **different axis** from ``PowerState`` and must never be conflated
with it.  ``PowerState`` is a *provenance* label (``measured`` /
``estimated`` / ``allocated`` / ``unknown``) derived by ``power_state_for``
from ``Source`` and ``MeasurementBasis``; ``PowerLevel`` is the *operating
level* the number sits at.  A value can be both ``measured`` and
``standby``: the two fields answer different questions and coexist on
``InferenceResult``.

``UNKNOWN`` is the neutral default, so a payload that does not name a level
reads as "not stated" rather than as a claim.
PowerLevel.title: PowerLevel

description:
The power block of a cell: contribution, bounds and operating state.

``estimated_power_w`` is ``None`` when the mapping is not observable or the
cell is group-only; it is never defaulted to ``0`` (HB §18).
title: CellPower
